title: flow-trace Sequence document
description: Object model for the Sequence mode (low-level, exact view): an ordered, nested record of real execution — which methods are called, in what order, with what params/request, what they return, and source refs. Rendered as a sequence diagram. A single *.sequence.json file is one Sequence document, linked from a Flow step via drill-down.

$schema.description: Optional pointer to this schema for editor/IDE validation. Ignored by flow-trace.

version.description: Schema version of this document, for migrations.

kind.description: Document kind discriminator. Always 'sequence' for a Sequence document.

id.description: Identity of THIS sequence. Workspace-unique across flows AND sequences. Stable, scoped id (e.g. 'charge-sequence'), not a display label.

title.description: Human-readable title of the sequence (display only).

overview.description: Optional document-level overview — general information about this sequence, as paragraphs (one per array item). Shown in the bottom Overview bar.

twin.description: Optional id of this document's TWIN — the SAME whole scenario at the other altitude (typically a Sequence paired with a Flow). A document-level link, DISTINCT from drill-down (which is part-of). Set it on both twins, each pointing to the other. The UI shows a Flow/Sequence toggle to switch between them.

actors.description: Participants = lifelines. Every participant, human AND system. Each call references actors as its caller (from) / callee (to). Drives lifeline color.

phases.description: Optional sections that group the sequence (rendered as separators).

calls.description: Ordered top-level calls. Each call may nest children (calls made during its activation). Pre-order traversal is the chronological order; nesting depth is the activation depth.

scopedId.description: Stable, scoped identifier: lowercase alphanumerics with '.', '_' or '-' as separators (e.g. 'txn.charge', 'charge-detail'). This is identity, NOT the display label.

id.description: Actor identity, referenced by call.from / call.to.

kind.description: Nature of the participant. human = external user/operator; system = external system/remote API; service = internal component/service; infra = database/queue/cache.

color.description: Optional explicit lifeline color (hex). If omitted, an auto-palette is used.

label.description: Display label for the section separator.

call.description: One call/message. Only 'to' and 'method' are required — the rest is optional, like a Flow node's content.

id.description: Call identity (unique across ALL calls in this sequence, including nested). Used for selection and cross-references.

from.description: Caller actor id (the lifeline the message starts from). Omit for an entry point.

to.description: Callee actor id (the lifeline the message arrives at).

method.description: What is called (e.g. 'PaymentAdapter.charge'). Display label of the message.

phase.description: Optional — the phase (section) this call belongs to.

description.description: Optional — what this call does, as a LIST OF POINTS (one thesis per item, rendered as bullets).

params.description: Optional — the arguments passed to the call.

returns.description: Optional — the named values the call returns.

returnType.description: Optional — the return type as a string (e.g. 'ChargeResult').

request.description: Optional — a request payload summary (e.g. 'POST /charge { amount, currency }').

response.description: Optional — a response payload summary (e.g. '{ id, status }').

source.description: Optional — a code reference for this call (file / symbol / line).

async.description: Optional — true for an asynchronous call (rendered with an open arrowhead). Default false (synchronous, solid arrow).

children.description: Optional — calls made during this call's activation (nested deeper). Pre-order over children continues the chronological sequence.
